Replay

Replay WebRTC adapter

6 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Connections and signalingPacket limits and flow controlAcceptance and remaining work

Use Rtc for Replay packets over WebRTC data channels, including browser gameplay. It owns raw Godot WebRTCPeerConnection and WebRTCDataChannel objects. It does not install MultiplayerAPI, use scene RPCs, or share a global session pool. Keep its address stable while open. rtc_transport exposes the same copied-packet interface used by ENet, server/client sessions and the P2P runner.

Odin
rtc: transportgd.Rtc
assert(transportgd.rtc_open(&rtc, {url = "wss://your-relay/rtc", host = true}))
wire := transportgd.rtc_transport(&rtc)
defer tr.close(&wire)
// Each frame: tr.poll(&wire), then drain tr.receive. rtc.room becomes available
// after registration. Join with {url = ..., room = shared_code}.

For the gameplay facade, start from SESSION_OPTIONS, set backend = .Rtc, rtc = {url = ..., room = ...}, and choose Host, Server, Client or Observer. session_frame pumps the transport; read the assigned code from session.rtc.room. Role controls whether registration creates or joins a room. Options' strings are copied by the adapter during opening and released on close. session_close owns transport teardown, including optional delay and recovery routing wrappers.

Connections and signaling#

The JSON signaling protocol uses create, join, signal and leave requests; responses are created/joined, peer, peer_left, signal and error. Introductions carry numeric peer IDs, and the lower ID creates the offer. The relay must introduce both endpoints before forwarding SDP/ICE and assign from from the authenticated socket, never a client-supplied sender. IDs must not be reused within a live room. A star relay gives host/client connections; a mesh relay gives direct connections between all introduced peers. There is no automatic game-packet forwarding between unconnected peers.

SDP uses {kind:"sdp", sdp_type:"offer"|"answer", sdp:...} under data. ICE uses {kind:"ice", media:..., index:..., name:...}. Incoming ICE waits until the remote description has actually been installed, including Godot's async answer path. Callback contexts remain alive through the custom Callable's final reference, are marked inactive before disconnect, and cannot target a reused connection slot after teardown.

The adapter has 16 remote slots, 32 KiB signaling messages, nesting depth 16, 64 pending ICE candidates per peer, a 15-second registration deadline and a 45-second handshake deadline. Signaling uses a bounded 128 KiB socket buffer and 64-message poll budget. It preserves healthy direct channels when signaling is lost and reports signaling_lost. Authenticated grant configuration enables signaling continuation with bounded identity reservations; plain relays retain explicit failure handling. It does not silently create another room.

ice_json supplies the WebRTC configuration, including deployment-specific STUN/TURN servers and credentials. The default is an empty ICE-server list for local testing. The local fixture in tests/replay_rtc/signal_server.mjs binds only to loopback; it is not a public authenticated room service. Browser-native WebRTC is the tested target. Native use explicitly requires native_extension = true and an installed Godot WebRTC extension; native ENet remains the default.

Party and the Cavecrawl/Scrapyard menus carry bounded, validated ICE settings through Room migration/rejoin. Actual Coturn UDP/TCP fixtures inspect selected relay candidates and transferred bytes; wrong credentials cannot fall back to direct gameplay in relay-only mode. See ICE deployment settings.

Packet limits and flow control#

Reliable and unreliable traffic use separately negotiated channels (IDs 0 and 1). The unreliable channel is unordered with zero retransmissions. Each physical packet is at most 1,200 bytes: a 16-byte credit envelope plus at most 1,184 bytes from the fragmentation layer. Logical Replay packets retain their 65,536-byte limit. The fragment header is 20 bytes, with a message ID, total length and part index/count; all integers are little endian. Fragments validate bounds before allocation and deliver reliable logical messages in send order.

New peers advertise control_stream: 1 alongside their SDP and use negotiated channel 2 (replay-control-v1) for cumulative credit acknowledgments and fences. This channel is reliable and unordered: older cumulative acknowledgments can be ignored safely, and fences already use a monotonic receive frontier. Application data remains on IDs 0/1 and keeps its existing ordering and sequence validation. The separate stream avoids waiting for ordered checkpoint messages to be delivered before credit messages become available. It still shares SCTP congestion control; it does not guarantee latency or solve all snapshot-freshness stalls under loss.

Absent the peer capability, controls retain their original reliable channel-0 path. Rtc_Config.legacy_control explicitly omits the capability and third channel. Receiving application data on control stream 2, control on unreliable stream 1, or an acknowledgment beyond the sender's issued sequence remains a protocol error. Channel 2 is required to open only after both local support and remote capability are known. This capability does not change the packet header, gameplay protocol, checkpoint format, identity or authority checks. Real mixed-version loaded-game handoffs cover both offerer/answerer directions; native-extension deployment and broader platform validation remain additional coverage.

The browser adapter requires Godot's network/limits/webrtc/max_channel_in_buffer_kb to be at least its default 64 KiB; smaller settings fail opening explicitly. The adapter limits each channel to 16 unacknowledged data packets and 32 KiB of local queued channel bytes. Acknowledgments follow application receipt, not merely SCTP delivery. This matters because Godot's JS data-channel ring can drop data even on a reliable channel when it fills. A reliable credit probe releases lost unreliable packets' window; it does not retransmit their gameplay payloads. An unacknowledged window closes after 15 seconds without credit progress, exposing a disconnection instead of silently claiming reliable delivery. Applications should continue polling/draining during menus; prolonged suspension requires reconnect.

Fragment queues default to 32 messages, 1 MiB outgoing and 2 MiB incoming logical bytes. Unfinished unreliable assemblies expire after two seconds. Reliable assemblies remain until consumed or disconnected; receive backpressure retains the next fragment. Buffer_Too_Small retains a complete logical packet for retry. Closing Fragments alone releases only its storage, borrowing its base transport; closing the public Rtc transport also closes its owned Godot objects.

Acceptance and remaining work#

Run nix develop --command bash tests/replay_rtc/run.sh with the Godot web templates, Chrome and the existing tests/web/node_modules dependencies installed. Failures retain logs; missing browser dependencies also fail the gate. The fixture uses separate Chrome processes and real data channels, without public STUN/TURN. It exchanges 64 KiB reliable messages followed by smaller messages, unreliable data, direct client-to-client traffic, departure, replacement and closing/reopening the same adapter address. A second scenario uses the ordinary Hello simulation through Session and compares canonical world hashes after movement and a reliable firing action.

Room supports challenged RTC destinations through Migration_Transport, using a trusted provider URL and a code derived from the signed authority view. Planned and killed-host Cavecrawl browser gates pass. Wider failure cases, public provisioning/TURN and additional browser engines remain open. See the authenticated signaling frontend. Replay Duel also provides P2P gameplay/spectator/archive gates; other ports still need browser acceptance.

Same-term Room reconnection can retain an authenticated RTC continuation across transport replacement, while requesting new channels and preserving the client's action ledger. Real Coturn outage tests exercise recovery without replacing the game processes or authority. See RTC recovery.

Engine contracts: WebRTCPeerConnection, WebRTCDataChannel, and Godot's JS receive/send implementation.

Authenticated signaling recovery uses resume_signaling and the provider's continuation token. signaling_resumes counts completed resumptions; rtc_connection_serial reports local peer-connection generations for diagnostics. rtc_drop_signaling closes only the signaling socket and is useful for embedding lifecycle controls or fault tests. If every existing channel is healthy, a resume preserves those generations and all data/fragment state. See rendezvous for challenge, grace-period and provider compatibility requirements.

An authenticated provider may attach exact 64-bit member and incarnation metadata to introductions. Rtc_Config.require_identity requires an authorization callback and refuses introductions missing valid identity metadata. rtc_peer_identity exposes that identity for a connected physical peer on an authenticated signaling connection. Applications still validate the member against their roster before creating a logical binding. See P2P admission for the fixed-match provider and rejoin integration.
